producer_report.summary: The plan check now sends back, with no critic call, an open question that asks whether existing tests break or what a backticked named function does on its failure or retry path. That holds even with a `User:` or `Host:` prefix. In `open_questions_findings` (admission.rs) this is a third `else if` branch calling a new helper, `asks_about_existing_behavior`. The helper strips the prefix first, then applies its exemptions to the question body: a first word of should/shall/would; acceptable/allowed/prefer(s)/wish; `user` followed by want/expect/prefer; toolchain/platform/machine/os/host. Doc comments on `open_questions_findings` and `plan_findings` list the rule, the exemptions, the known misses and the ~3% estimate (labelled an estimate). planner.md now has a bullet requiring `file:line` for each claim about existing code, and it makes the dependents search explicit. It stays at 2383 bytes, so the docs/system-facts.md budget line is unchanged. Tests added: three admission unit tests, 15 refusal-corpus cases, and a job_plan.rs scripted planner/critic test. In that test the planner is called twice, the critic once, and critique 1 is the critic's own. planning.rs changed by comment only. fake.rs is unchanged on purpose.

open_issues: The ~3% refusal-rate figure is the reading's estimate. I did not measure it, and the replay of readings does not apply because the rule governs plans.

Known misses are listed in the doc comment and not refused: 'should existing tests ...' phrasing, questions naming a platform or toolchain, unbackticked function names, and 'does the suite still pass?'.
mistakes: My first clippy run put `-q` after `--`, so clippy-driver rejected it; I reran with `--quiet` before `--`. No code was affected.
learnings: Bash hooks here allow only cargo, chmod, git, ls, mv and rm. Pipes to tail, head, grep or rg and echo are refused, so use `cargo ... -q` and read files with the Read and Grep tools.
`cargo clippy -q` fails: the flag is passed through to clippy-driver after `--`. Use `--quiet` before the `--`.
planner.md is composed into the planner frame through `include_str!`, and the budgets test compares ceil(bytes/3) with the docs/system-facts.md line. A byte-neutral edit keeps that test green.
